correctness.rationale: The free ball is the edge-root hull: the molecule of a missing matching edge is an average of two adjacent edge roots. In H the active dual equations have rank 2k−1 exactly when the tight graph connects all vertices. Such a potential has integer differences and range at most two; range two forces opposite extremes in one pair with every other value intermediate. Thus all dual vertices are special potentials or centered binary cuts. The original Q and its inverse give the squared distortion product; scaling the primal radius and averaging by convexity of the inverse quadratic energies loses nothing. Independent swaps remove off-block terms, and pair permutations make each block scalar, with every edge root having squared block norms (1,1). A cut with h ones and r split pairs has total energy h(2k−h)/(2k) and U-energy r/2. For k≥4 these and the special energy 2 give the upper bound k at α=1/2. For even k the balanced all-split and whole-pair cuts match it; for odd k the all-split and one-split balanced cuts bound the two sides of 1/2. These witnesses are feasible even without the vertex argument. For k=2,3 the crossed lower bounds 2/α and W-energy 1 or 4/3 divided by 1−α meet at 2/3 and 3/5; the cut energy bound, using parity of r when h=3 for k=3, matches them. The argument holds for all real linear isomorphisms but only identifies the invariant optimizer.

It tests candidate energies only; the witnesses and averaging certify global optima.
